title: Modules never gate a row write on the framework-managed owner column by hand
intent: Object-level authorization is applied centrally: the framework stamps owner_id from the request actor on create and authorizes every update / delete of an owned row at the write chokepoint (a non-owner write fails closed with 403). A module that references owner_id — to compare it against a principal, filter on it, or set it — is hand-rolling that per-row check, the easy-to-get-wrong pattern the seam replaces (it leaks if forgotten, and a hand-written ownership filter also drops the soft-delete / tenant row scope). Declare the ownership trait on the model and let the framework gate the write; register an object-authorization predicate for a richer policy. As with the scope / actor columns, a read DTO may still expose owner_id (an annotation is fine); only attribute access (set / filter / compare) is policed.
reference: OwnedMixin declares ownership; BaseService stamps owner_id and apply_object_authz gates writes (ADR 0029); a custom object-authz predicate can be registered.

runtime.rationale: Every update/delete of an owned row is authorized per-row at the write chokepoint (apply_object_authz; a non-owner write fails closed with 403), and owner_id is stamped centrally on create -- the authorization a manual check would hand-roll is guaranteed by the framework.
